title: A data-driven framework for agent-based modeling of vehicular travel using publicly available data
authors: Yirong Zhou; Xiaoyue Cathy Liu; Bingkun Chen; Tony Grubesic; Ran Wei; Danielle Wallace
abstract: This study presents a methodology for creating a synthetic travel demand, encompassing households and individuals and their daily activities, to support agent-based modeling (ABM) in urban planning and travel analysis. Unlike previous studies, which often rely on proprietary data, our approach is entirely based on open data, ensuring replicability by the broader research community. The research is among the first to propose the entire framework for travel demand synthesis and ABM. Results are validated against ground truth from the Census and other public data sources. The ABM results are compared to an Information Minimization (IM) model, which is an aggregated model capturing commuting patterns by race. The study contributes to the field by offering a comprehensive and replicable data foundation for ABM, serving as a valuable resource for evaluating population and travel demand synthesis algorithms.
abstractZh: 本研究提出一种合成出行需求的方法，涵盖家庭、个体及其日常活动，以支持城市规划和出行分析中的基于智能体建模（ABM）。与经常依赖专有数据的既有研究不同，本方法完全基于开放数据，使更广泛的研究群体能够复现。该研究是较早提出完整出行需求合成与ABM框架的研究之一。研究结果通过人口普查及其他公共数据来源的真实观测进行验证，并将ABM结果与信息最小化（IM）模型进行比较；后者是一种按种族刻画通勤模式的聚合模型。本研究提供了全面且可复现的ABM数据基础，可作为评估人口合成和出行需求合成算法的重要资源。
